diagnostic_evidence.quote: assume that $\mathbf{G}=\mathbf{A}(\mathbb{I}_1,\mathbb{I}_2)$ has the maximal volume among all $S_1\times S_2$ submatrices of $\mathbf{A}$ with $\mathbf{G}$ being full column rank
we choose two index sets $\mathbb{T}_n'=[-kb_n:-(k-1)b_n-1]\cup[(k-1)b_n+1:kb_n]$
We provided theoretical error bounds, ensuring the approximation quality is controllable and on par with the standard method when the coefficient matrix is low-rank.
Theoretical bounds on the approximation error are provided, ensuring the reliability of our methods.

issues.failure_explanation: The abstract (repeated in the introduction and conclusion) claims theoretical error bounds for both proposed approaches, ensuring rigorous control of the approximation quality. What the paper actually proves: Theorem 3.4 is an existence statement for some low-rank factorization, and Theorem 4.1 with cor:added-1 is conditional on the selected core G = A(I_1,I_2) having maximal volume among all S_1xS_2 submatrices of A. The second, adaptive approach (Algorithms 1 and 2) grows the index sets by fixed symmetric blocks with a sigma_min stopping heuristic; no theorem anywhere bounds the error of the 3-tuple these algorithms return, and nothing shows the adaptively produced core is maximal-volume. So the claimed guarantee for the adaptive approach is unsupported.

failure_location.quote: Theoretical error bounds are derived for both approaches, ensuring rigorous control over approximation quality.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the abstract/introduction/conclusion to state that error bounds are proved only for (existence and) maximal-volume index selection, and present the adaptive algorithms as heuristic with experimental support; alternatively add a genuinely new analysis of the greedy block-CUR output. The least resolution the source supports is the claim restriction.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised rigorous error control for the paper's main practical (adaptive) algorithms is unsubstantiated; their accuracy rests only on numerical experiments. The claim additionally leans on Theorem 3.4/cor:added-1, which are defective in their own right (separate issues).
issues.title: Advertised error bounds do not cover the adaptive algorithms
issues.why_classification: Restricting the prose is a contained repair needing no new proof architecture and leaving the paper (matrix-level CUR theory, two algorithms, experiments) recognizably intact, but it downgrades the flagship adaptive method from provably controlled to heuristic, which exceeds a routine local fix.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Therefore, the proof is complete by combining Theorems \ref{t-lasso:general-theorem-main} and \ref{t-lasso:epsilonrank-main}.
when we assume that $\min\{I_1,I_2\}\geq (C|f(x_1,x_2)|_{\alpha}/\epsilon)^{1/\alpha}$, one has that $\|Ff(x_1,x_2)-f(x_1,x_2)\|_{L^2}\leq \epsilon$

issues.failure_explanation: The only ingredient for the truncation term is Theorem 3.1, which provides C*min{I_1,I_2}^{-alpha}|f|_alpha (the paper's own remark after Theorem 3.1 also uses min). The statement of Theorem 3.4 upgrades min to max, a strictly stronger and false claim: for f(x_1,x_2) = e^{i(I_1+1)x_1} one has Ff = 0 and ||Ff-f||_{L^2} = 1, the coefficient matrix A over [-I_1,I_1]x[-I_2,I_2] is zero (so the epsilon*||A||_2 term vanishes and a rank-R factorization of arbitrarily small norm exists), and |f|_alpha = (I_1+1)^alpha; with I_1 fixed and I_2 -> infinity the claimed right-hand side C*I_2^{-alpha}(I_1+1)^alpha tends to 0, contradicting the bound. cor:added-1 repeats the same max-term.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace max{I_1,I_2} by min{I_1,I_2} in both statements, matching Theorem 3.1.
issues.overall_effect: The truncation-rate term of Theorem 3.4 and of cor:added-1 is wrong whenever I_1 differs from I_2, promising an unearned decay governed by the larger truncation order.
issues.title: Truncation term upgraded from min{I_1,I_2} to max{I_1,I_2} in Theorem 3.4
issues.why_classification: A forced one-symbol correction restores the standard rate; the paper's own remark uses min, the algorithms and numerics take I_1 = I_2 (where min = max), and no inference or construction needs repair.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \widetilde{F}f(x_1,x_2)-Ff(x_1,x_2)=\sum_{i_1=1}^{2I_1+1}\sum_{i_2=1}^{2I_2+1}(\mathbf{A}(i_1,i_2)-(\mathbf{E}\mathbf{F}^*)(i_1,i_2))e^{\iota\cdot k_1x_1} e^{\iota \cdot k_2x_2}
\|\widetilde{\mathbf{A}}-\mathbf{A}\|_{\max}\leq \epsilon\|\mathbf{A}\|_2,
where $R=\lceil 72\ln(2(I_1+I_2)+3)/\epsilon^2\rceil$.

issues.failure_explanation: The basis {e^{ik_1x_1}e^{ik_2x_2}} is orthonormal under the paper's inner product, so by the paper's own Parseval identity ||F~f - Ff||_{L^2}^2 equals sum_{i_1,i_2} |(A-EF*)(i_1,i_2)|^2 = ||A-EF*||_F^2: the L^2 error EQUALS the Frobenius norm of the coefficient error. The proof asserts it is at most the max norm, which is the wrong direction: ||M||_F can exceed ||M||_max by a factor up to sqrt((2I_1+1)(2I_2+1)). Hence the conclusion epsilon*||A||_2 (imported from Theorem 3.3's max-norm estimate) is unjustified. The statement is in fact false at the prescribed rank: take f a trigonometric polynomial whose coefficient matrix is sigma*H on the (2m+1)x(2m+1) modes {-m,...,m}^2 with H orthogonal (e.g., Hadamard), I_1 = I_2 = m^3, alpha = 2, and epsilon chosen so that R = ceil(72 ln(2(I_1+I_2)+3)/epsilon^2) is about m. Then Ff = f, every rank-<=R factorization satisfies ||F~f - f||_{L^2} = ||A~ - A||_F >= sigma*sqrt(2m+1-R), while C*max^{-2}|f|_2 + epsilon*||A||_2 = o(sigma) as m grows; so no admissible E,F realize the claimed bound. The same false inequality is the sole step converting Theorem 4.1's max-norm CUR estimate into the L^2 statement of cor:added-1, which fails on the same example (with S_1 = S_2 = 1 it claims error <= 2 sigma_2(A) + o(1), but every rank-1 approximant has Frobenius error at least sigma*sqrt(2m)).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: The only source-supported repair replaces the false step by the Parseval/Frobenius identity, yielding valid bounds with an extra factor sqrt((2I_1+1)(2I_2+1)) multiplying epsilon*||A||_2 (Theorem 3.4) and multiplying sqrt(1+S_2)sqrt(1+S_2/(S_1-S_2+1)) sigma_{S_2+1}(A) (cor:added-1); keeping total error O(epsilon) then forces tolerance O(epsilon/sqrt(I_1 I_2)) and hence rank and sample budgets comparable to the full coefficient count. Preserving a dimension-free bound would require new hypotheses (singular-value decay, or a Frobenius-norm approximate rank) absent from the source.
issues.overall_effect: The paper's central guarantees collapse: L^2 accuracy epsilon*||A||_2 at rank R = O(epsilon^{-2} ln(I_1+I_2)) (Theorem 3.4) and O(sigma_{S_2+1}(A)) accuracy of the maximal-volume CUR approximation of f (cor:added-1) are unachievable in general. These results motivate the entire CUR-sampling program and underlie the error-control claims in the abstract, Section 4 and the conclusion.
issues.title: L^2 error bounded by max-norm where Parseval gives the (larger) Frobenius norm
issues.why_classification: Every supported resolution either attaches a dimension-growing factor that voids the advertised accuracy-versus-integrals guarantee (a central guarantee and rate materially worsens) or requires essentially new rank theory; the stated bound fails even for the best rank-R approximation, so no comparable version of the claim survives as written.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \STATE Select $\mathbb{T}_n'=[-kb_n:-(k-1)b_n-1]\cup[(k-1)b_n+1:kb_n]$ with $n=1,2$.
\STATE Select $\mathbb{T}_n=\{0\}$ with $n=1,2$.
For given two integers $a$ and $b$ with $a<b$, we use $[a:b]$ to denote the set $\{a,a+1,\dots,b-1,b\}$.
with $S_n=2Kb_n+1$ with $n=1,2$.

issues.failure_explanation: The counter is initialized at k = 0 and used directly in the block formula, so the first iteration selects T_n' = [0:b_n-1] union [1-b_n:0] = {1-b_n,...,b_n-1} (by the paper's [a:b] notation), which contains 0 and therefore overlaps the initial T_n = {0}. The updated C = [C, C_0] and R = [R; R_0] then contain the zero-frequency column/row twice (in Algorithms 2 and 3 the assembled core G gets a duplicated zero row and column), forcing sigma_min(C) = sigma_min(R) = 0, so the stopping statistic tol is 0 from the first iteration onward and the tau-test carries no information. In addition the first block contributes only 2b_n-1 new indices, so after the loop the index sets have size 2(K+1)b_n, contradicting the stated S_n = 2Kb_n+1 and the integral/operation counts built on it. The prose intends k >= 1 (disjoint blocks of 2b_n indices); the same off-by-one is hard-coded in Algorithms 2 and 3.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Initialize k = 1 (equivalently shift the block formula by one), as presupposed by the prose description and by the claimed block sizes.
issues.overall_effect: As written, all three algorithms run with a degenerate, always-satisfied convergence statistic (tau is ineffective) and produce index sets whose sizes differ from the claimed S_n = 2Kb_n+1, so the derived counts of double integrals and operations do not describe the written procedures.
issues.title: Loop counter initialized at k=0 so the first index block duplicates the zero mode
issues.why_classification: A forced, local index correction: after it the blocks are disjoint, the stopping statistic is non-degenerate, and every stated size and cost count holds, with no claim or guarantee changed.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: a tolerance $0<\tau<1$, and the maximum number of iterations $K$.
if $\max\{\sigma_{\min}(\mathbf{C})^2/{\rm nF}_{\mathbf{C}},\sigma_{\min}(\mathbf{R})^2/{\rm nF}_{\mathbf{R}}\}< \tau^2$ is not satisfied, then we continue Steps (a)-(d)
\WHILE{${\rm tol}>\tau$ or $k\leq K$}

issues.failure_explanation: A loop governed by 'tol > tau or k <= K' exits only when both disjuncts fail, i.e., only when tol <= tau AND k > K. The written loop therefore (i) cannot stop before completing K+1 iterations, even if the convergence tolerance has already been met, and (ii) never terminates if tol remains above tau, so the quantity K - advertised in the input as 'the maximum number of iterations' - acts as a minimum and provides no termination guarantee. The prose describes continuing only while the tau-condition fails, i.e., stopping upon convergence. The same defective connective appears in Algorithms 2 and 3 (t-lasso:alg2-main, t-lasso:alg1:app-main).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace 'or' by 'and' in the while-condition (continue while tol > tau and k <= K).
issues.overall_effect: The written algorithms may ignore convergence for K+1 iterations or fail to terminate at all, so the claimed iteration cap, the sizes S_n = 2Kb_n+1, and the integral/operation counts that assume at most K iterations do not hold for the procedures as written.
issues.title: While-loop uses 'or', making K a minimum and losing termination guarantee
issues.why_classification: A one-token repair restores the stated input-output contract (stop on convergence or after K iterations); all guarantees and counts then match the prose, with no mathematical content lost.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: if $\max\{\sigma_{\min}(\mathbf{C})^2/{\rm nF}_{\mathbf{C}},\sigma_{\min}(\mathbf{R})^2/{\rm nF}_{\mathbf{R}}\}< \tau^2$ is not satisfied, then we continue Steps (a)-(d), where $0<\tau<1$ is a given parameter.

issues.failure_explanation: The prose stopping rule is a max-criterion: iterate until max{sigma_min(C)^2/nF_C, sigma_min(R)^2/nF_R} < tau^2, i.e., until BOTH relative smallest singular values are below tau. The algorithm instead sets tol = min{sigma_min(C)/sqrt(nF_C), sigma_min(R)/sqrt(nF_R)} and stops when tol <= tau, i.e., as soon as ONE of the two factors meets the test. The two specifications of the same procedure contradict each other; under the min-rule the iteration can terminate when only one of C, R has converged by the paper's own criterion, returning a CUR triple whose other factor still violates it.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use tol = max{sigma_min(C)/sqrt(nF_C), sigma_min(R)/sqrt(nF_R)} (equivalently the prose's squared max-condition).
issues.overall_effect: Algorithm 1 as written does not implement its stated stopping rule and can stop with one factor un-converged, so the returned 3-tuple need not satisfy the convergence property the paper describes for the procedure.
issues.title: Stopping statistic uses min while the prose specifies max
issues.why_classification: A local one-word change aligns the algorithm with its own prose specification; the intended heuristic behavior and all other claims are preserved.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: the number of double integrals in Algorithm \ref{t-lasso:alg1:app-main} is less than Algorithms \ref{t-lasso:alg1-main} and \ref{t-lasso:alg2-main}.
\STATE Compute $\mathbf{C}$ according to (\ref{t-lasso:method-one:sub1-main}) with $\mathbb{T}_2$, and $\mathbf{R}$ according to (\ref{t-lasso:method-one:sub2-main}) with $\mathbb{T}_1$.
Therefore, Algorithm \ref{t-lasso:alg2-main} needs $(2I_1+1)S_2+(2I_2+1)S_1-S_1S_2$ double integrals to obtain the 3-tuple $\{\mathbf{C},\mathbf{U},\mathbf{R}\}$
$\mathbf{G}_{1k}\in\mathbb{C}^{(2(k-1)b_1+1)\times 2b_2}$, $\mathbf{G}_{2k}\in\mathbb{C}^{2b_1\times (2(k-1)b_2+1)}$ and $\mathbf{G}_{3k}\in\mathbb{C}^{2b_1\times 2b_2}$

issues.failure_explanation: Algorithm 3 zeroes the off-diagonal blocks of the core (G_{1k} = G_{2k} = 0) but still computes the full factors C in C^{(2I_1+1)xS_2} and R in C^{S_1x(2I_2+1)}, and every entry of C and R - including the whole S_1xS_2 overlap region C(I_1,:) = R(:,I_2), whose off-block-diagonal entries are genuine Fourier coefficients - is consumed by the product C*U*R. The number of distinct double integrals is therefore (2I_1+1)S_2 + (2I_2+1)S_1 - S_1S_2, exactly as for Algorithms 1 and 2. The claimed smaller count is attainable only by skipping (equivalently, zeroing) the off-block-diagonal overlap entries inside C and R, which yields a different approximation that no error analysis covers. Even under that reading the printed formula is inconsistent with the paper's own block dimensions: the block-diagonal core built in the loop has 1 + 4Kb_1b_2 entries (one 1x1 block and K blocks of size 2b_1 x 2b_2), not Kb_1b_2.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the count to (2I_1+1)S_2 + (2I_2+1)S_1 - S_1S_2 and withdraw the 'less than' claim (the modification then only offers cheaper per-iteration sigma_min updates through the block-diagonal core), or else specify and analyze the genuinely different approximation obtained by zeroing the off-block-diagonal overlap coefficients.
issues.overall_effect: The appendix's advertised advantage - that the modification needs strictly fewer double integrals than Algorithms 1 and 2, quantified by the printed formula - is not achieved, so the efficiency motivation and comparison for the modified algorithm are unreliable.
issues.title: Appendix Algorithm 3's claimed reduction in double integrals is impossible as stated
issues.why_classification: The least resolution withdraws the modification's advertised integral savings - a substantive promise, so not minor - but keeps the algorithm, its block-structure work savings, and its numerical comparisons, a limited weakening that requires no new global theory.
